report.summary: Checkout is failing because the database connection pool (size 10, overflow 0) is exhausted by transactions that were left open. Eight connections are idle-in-transaction, the oldest for about 21 minutes, and 37 requests are waiting. The log shows checkout.create_order holding a connection for 420s. The pool-exhaustion errors directly cause the checkout 500s and the degraded health check.
report.root_cause: Long-running idle-in-transaction DB sessions opened by checkout.create_order hold all 10 pool connections, so new checkout requests time out waiting for a connection (QueuePool limit reached, timeout 30s). The likely code origin is the v2.15.0 change "Refactor order creation to use a single transaction", but that deploy went out on 2026-11-08, about a day before the incident, so it does not explain the onset by itself. The specific trigger (for example, a slow external call made inside the open transaction) was not confirmed.

evidence.finding: demo-app returns HTTP 503, status 'degraded', latency 30000 ms.

'QueuePool limit of size 10 overflow 0 reached, connection timed out, timeout 30.00' (15:22:26Z and 15:42:26Z); 'POST /checkout 500 TimeoutError: could not acquire DB connection' (15:23:26Z, 15:27:26Z).
pool_size 10, active 10, idle 0, idle_in_transaction 8, waiting_requests 37, longest_transaction_s 1260, oldest_idle_in_transaction_s 1260.
WARN at 15:16:26Z: 'slow transaction detected: checkout.create_order held connection 420s'.
Latest deploy v2.15.0 (2026-11-08T09:47:26Z) 'Refactor order creation to use a single transaction', no config changes. Previous deploy v2.14.0 was 2026-11-06.
CPU 12%, memory 48%, disk 41%. Host resources are not the constraint.
db_pool_size 10, db_pool_timeout_s 30. No recent config change; the pool is small.

db-connection-pool runbook: find transactions held open and the code path holding them; terminate long-idle sessions as short-term relief; make sure transactions are closed before slow external calls; raise pool size only after fixing leaks.

recommended_steps: Short term: terminate the 8 idle-in-transaction sessions older than about 20 minutes on the DB to free the pool, then confirm checkout recovers.

Identify which code path inside checkout.create_order holds the transaction open. Check whether a slow external call (payment or inventory) runs inside the transaction, and move it outside the transaction boundary.
Review the v2.15.0 order-creation transaction refactor and consider rolling it back if the leak is confirmed there.
Add an idle_in_transaction_session_timeout and alerting on the idle-in-transaction count. Raise the pool size only after the leak is fixed.

report.root_cause: Database transactions in the checkout order-creation path are not being closed. Connections stay in "idle in transaction" state, so the pool of size 10 (overflow 0) runs out and new checkout requests wait 30s and then fail with "could not acquire DB connection". The likely trigger is checkout.create_order holding its transaction open across a slow step, possibly an external call. The most recent related change is v2.15.0 (Nov 8, "Refactor order creation to use a single transaction"). That release is about a day old, so it does not clearly match the 30-minute start, and the exact code path that holds the transaction is not confirmed.

Connections stay in "idle in transaction" state, so the pool of size 10 (overflow 0) runs out and new checkout requests wait 30s and then fail with "could not acquire DB connection". The likely trigger is checkout.create_order holding its transaction open across a slow step, possibly an external call. The most recent related change is v2.15.0 (Nov 8, "Refactor order creation to use a single transaction"). That release is about a day old, so it does not clearly match the 30-minute start, and the exact code path that holds the transaction is not confirmed.</root_cause>
<parameter name="category">db_connection_pool_exhausted

recommended_steps: Short-term relief: a DBA or on-call engineer should terminate the sessions that have been idle in transaction for more than a few minutes (pg_terminate_backend on those pids), then confirm the pool recovers and checkout succeeds.

Find the code path: inspect checkout.create_order (introduced in v2.15.0's single-transaction refactor) for a transaction that stays open across an external call such as payment or inventory. Commit or close the transaction before making slow external calls.
Consider rolling back to v2.14.0 if the leak is confirmed in v2.15.0 and the fix will take time. Check whether the 30-minute start lines up with a traffic change or a payment/inventory slowdown.
Add a transaction timeout (idle_in_transaction_session_timeout) on the database and alerting on idle-in-transaction count and pool wait time.
Only after the leak is fixed, consider raising db_pool_size. Do not raise it as the first fix.

report.summary: Payment failures started with the v2.15.1 release at 15:25Z. The release changed payment_service_url from https://payments.internal/v1 to https://payments.internall/v1 (note the extra "l"). Checkout requests fail with a DNS error because the hostname does not resolve. The payment service itself is healthy.
report.root_cause: A typo in the payment_service_url config value introduced by release v2.15.1 (author sam, "Update service endpoints for new region"). The hostname is payments.internall instead of payments.internal, so shop-api cannot resolve it and POST /checkout returns 500.

evidence.finding: v2.15.1 at 2026-11-09T15:25:46Z by sam: config_changes payment_service_url from "https://payments.internal/v1" to "https://payments.internall/v1". The previous release v2.14.0 (2026-11-06) had no config changes.
3 ERROR lines, all POST /checkout 500: "ConnectionError: Name or service not known: payments.internall" (at 15:27:46, 15:30:46, 15:44:46Z).
Live config shows payment_service_url: "https://payments.internall/v1", confirming the typo is in effect.
payment-service returned HTTP 200, status healthy (80 ms), so the payment service is up and the failure is on the caller side resolving the hostname.
demo-app returned HTTP 500, status degraded, consistent with checkout failures.

Check whether the 'new region' endpoint in the release notes needs a different hostname, and make sure the intended value is used, not just the typo fixed.
Add a deploy-pipeline check that validates dependency hostnames resolve before release, and add a config diff review for URL changes.

payload.summary: Product pages are slow and intermittently return 500s because calls to inventory-service are timing out (5s timeout). inventory-service itself reports degraded with about 9.4s health latency. The local DB pool and host resources are healthy, and no deployment occurred.
payload.root_cause: Upstream dependency slowness: inventory-service is responding slowly (calls took 5100ms and 9100ms per logs; health probe latency 9400ms, status 'degraded'). shop-api's inventory_timeout_s of 5 causes ReadTimeout errors on product endpoints such as /products/42 and /products/7, which return 500.

evidence.finding: demo-app returned HTTP 200 but status 'degraded' with latency_ms 5300.
inventory-service returned HTTP 200 with status 'degraded' and latency_ms 9400.
ERROR lines: 'GET /products/42 500 ReadTimeout: inventory-service (timeout=5s)' at 15:18:50Z and 'GET /products/7 500 ReadTimeout: inventory-service (timeout=5s)' at 15:33:50Z.
WARN lines: 'inventory-service call took 5100ms' at 15:13:50Z and 'inventory-service call took 9100ms' at 15:44:50Z.
inventory_timeout_s: 5, inventory_service_url: https://inventory.internal/v2.
pool_size 10, active 3, idle 4, idle_in_transaction 0, waiting_requests 0, longest_transaction_s 2. DB pool is not the bottleneck.
cpu_pct 22, mem_used_pct 48, disk_used_pct 41. Host resources healthy.

recommended_steps: Escalate to the inventory-service owning team with the latency evidence (9.4s health latency, 9.1s call durations) and investigate why inventory-service is slow (its DB, load, dependencies).
As short-term mitigation, consider a circuit breaker or fallback/cached inventory data for product pages so slow inventory calls do not produce 500s (per runbook slow-upstream-dependency).
Review the 5s inventory timeout and retry settings so slow calls do not exhaust web workers.
Confirm the DB pool issue is ruled out (it is currently healthy) before changing pool size.

report.summary: Product page slowness and 500s are caused by the upstream inventory-service being degraded (latency 5–9.4s), which exceeds shop-api's 5s inventory timeout. Local app resources, DB pool and recent deploys are not the cause.
report.root_cause: Upstream inventory-service is slow. Calls from shop-api to inventory.internal time out at the configured 5s, causing ReadTimeout 500s on product pages and slow responses while waiting.

recommended_steps: Escalate to the inventory-service owning team with the latency evidence (5.1s to 9.4s calls, health reports degraded) and check its own dashboards, DB and saturation.
Consider a circuit breaker or fallback for inventory data on product pages so that slow inventory calls do not tie up app workers or return 500s.
Review the 5s inventory_timeout_s and retry settings so slow calls fail fast and do not exhaust workers; consider a graceful degraded response instead of a 500.
Monitor demo-app and inventory-service health and the frequency of ReadTimeout errors until inventory latency recovers.
Note: the log sample is small (2 ERROR and 2 WARN lines), so the full error rate was not measured.
